mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A fall in the unemployment rate below 5.0% triggers increased consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE does not fall below 5.0% in the period, or returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising GDP growth (GDPC1) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals robust economic activity, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: The combination of GDPC1 rising above 18000 and UNRATE falling below 5.0% does not persist over the horizon, or 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate reduces equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS do not rise above 4.0% in the tightening cycle, or returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A drop in industrial production below its base index (INDPRO < 100) indicates weakening supply chains, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above 100, or returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) signals labor market uncertainty, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS do not increase over the 5-day horizon, or returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of falling unemployment (UNRATE) and falling federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) signals improved labor market conditions and accommodative monetary policy, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
regime_hint: improving labor market and easing monetary policy
failure_condition: The combination of UNRATE falling below 5.0% and FEDFUNDS below 4.0% does not occur, or returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the CPI inflation index above 2.5% triggers higher interest rates, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL does not exceed 2.5% over the 60-day period, or returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
